business_rules: Password changes are prevented if the current password is incorrect, the new password is not confirmed correctly, or the new password is the same as the previous one. (RF-06)
Vacation requests with an invalid date range are prevented. (RF-09)
Vacation requests that exceed an employee's available vacation balance are prevented. (RF-10)
Vacation balance is calculated using only business days, excluding weekends and holidays. (RF-11)
Annual vacation entitlement is calculated proportionally when an employee is in the first year of their contract. (RF-12)
Only approved vacation requests are considered when deducting from the vacation balance. (RF-13)
The total billing amount is automatically calculated from detailed items. (RF-38)
The net amount payable is automatically calculated when individual income-tax withholding applies to self-employed suppliers. (RF-39)
The primary due date of a billing record reflects the date of the last scheduled payment. (RF-41)
The outstanding billing balance is automatically calculated based on associated financial transactions. (RF-44)
A billing record is marked as paid when the financial transactions cover the total amount due. (RF-45)
The association with a credit instrument may create a new due date or not, according to the user's choice. (RF-47)
A dedicated document category is automatically created and maintained for each user. (RF-52)
Public notices are displayed at the system entry point. (RF-56)
A textual history of changes throughout the order workflow is preserved. (RF-61)
Critical business calculations are automatically performed, such as vacation balance, total billing amount, outstanding balance, withholdings, and final due date. (RNF-70)
Consistency is maintained between related modules, such as a user and their document folder, a proposal and billing, and billing and a credit instrument. (RNF-71)
Document versions and a history of changes are preserved in processes that require traceability, such as documents and commissions. (RNF-72)

microservices.responsibility: Maintain supporting master data such as departments, contract types, user categories, organization types, interaction types, tax reasons, billing schemes, and frequencies.
Manage users, access profiles, employment agreements, password management, and personal settings.
Enforce access control by user profile and scope, support local and LDAP authentication, and apply security to critical entities.
Record and manage vacation requests, calculate balances, control lifecycle, and notify approvers.
Manage organizations, contacts, external collaborators, job roles, interaction types, interactions, and proposals including lifecycle, composition, duplication, and conversion to billing.
Register and maintain projects associated with clients, including active period, status, involved roles, and related costs.

Record internal and external activities, classify billable/non-billable, distinguish workday time, maintain objectives and allocations, produce consolidated reports, and manage evidence with policies and alerts.

Maintain accounts, transaction types/groups, recurring transactions; record receivables/payables; detail billing records; calculate totals, withholdings, outstanding balances, and paid status; manage due dates and credit instruments; import billable hours and project costs; track financial indicators.

Organize documents by category, maintain versions, associate with responsible people and areas, auto-create per-user document categories, and maintain publications, notice boards, and other supporting content.

Record orders and commissions linked to projects, reviewers, collaborators, and payment data; control workflow states; record delays, changes, and files; preserve textual history; send documents by email.
Send email notifications for relevant business events such as vacation requests, contract expiry, password reset, pending evidence, and orders.
Provide reports by business domain and export in multiple formats including CSV, PDF, HTML, RTF, XLS, and ODT.

issues.description: The Master Data Service aggregates many unrelated reference-data types (departments, contract types, user categories, organization types, interaction types, tax reasons, billing schemes, frequencies) into a single service. The domain analysis lists 'Supporting master data administration' as one capability, but the entities span HR, CRM, and Finance domains, and the structural evidence shows these are managed by different manager packages (manager.admin, manager.contacts, manager.billing). A single service for all reference data creates a broad, low-cohesion boundary and a shared dependency hub.
evidence: RF-01 lists departments, contract types, user categories, organization types, interaction types, tax reasons, billing schemes, and frequencies as supporting master data.
Domain analysis capability 'Supporting master data administration' (RF-01, RF-ADM-04).
Structural analysis shows separate manager packages: manager.admin, manager.contacts, manager.billing.
issues.recommendation: Split master data by the domain that owns it (e.g., HR master data, CRM master data, Finance master data) or explicitly justify a single shared reference-data service with a clear ownership and change-management rationale.

issues.description: The User Management Service combines user/access-profile administration, employment-agreement management, password management, and personal settings. The domain analysis treats 'Employment agreement management' (RF-03), 'User and access profile management' (RF-04), and 'Password management' (RF-05, RF-06) as distinct capabilities. Employment agreements have their own lifecycle rules (annual workload, vacation allowance) and are referenced by vacation balance calculations, so mixing them with user administration weakens cohesion and creates overlapping responsibility with the Vacation Management Service for vacation entitlement data.
evidence: RF-03: maintain employment agreements with rules over a period, including annual workload and vacation allowance.
RF-04: register and maintain users with personal and contractual data, department, category, access profile, and employment agreement.
RF-05/RF-06: password change, reset, renewal, and validation rules.
Domain analysis separates 'Employment agreement management', 'User and access profile management', and 'Password management'.
issues.recommendation: Consider separating employment-agreement management (and possibly password/credential management) from user profile administration, or explicitly document why they must remain together and how vacation entitlement data is owned.

issues.description: The Security and Access Control Service is declared as a service and is listed as a communication target by User Management, Document Management, Finance and Billing, CRM, Project Management, Activity and Time Reporting, and Order and Commission. However, several services that manage critical entities subject to access control (e.g., Vacation Management Service for vacation requests, Notification Service for notifications, Reporting Service for reports, Master Data Service for reference data) do not declare communication with it. RNF-69 requires access control to be applied to documents, billing records, users, and other critical entities, so all services exposing critical entities should interact with the security service.
evidence: RNF-69: apply access control to documents, billing records, users, and other critical entities.
RNF-66/RNF-67: access control by user profile and scope of responsibility.
Candidate Security and Access Control Service communicates with only 7 of the 12 services; Vacation Management, Notification, Reporting, and Master Data do not list it.
issues.recommendation: Add Security and Access Control Service as a communication target for all services that expose or mutate critical entities, or clarify that access control is enforced at a gateway/API layer rather than per service.

issues.description: The Notification Service is responsible for sending email notifications for business events including contract expiry, but the User Management Service (which owns employment agreements and contract data) does not declare communication with the Notification Service. RF-15 requires email notification when contracts or probation periods are approaching expiry, and RF-73 lists contract expiry among notification events. Without an interaction from User Management (or an employment-agreement service) to Notification, this capability cannot be realized.
evidence: RF-15: send email notification when contracts or probation periods are approaching expiry.
RNF-73: email notifications for relevant business events, including contract expiry.
Candidate User Management Service communicates with Master Data, Security, Vacation Management, and Document Management, but not Notification Service.
issues.recommendation: Add Notification Service as a communication target of the User Management Service (or the service that owns employment agreements) for contract/probation expiry events.

issues.description: The Reporting Service is responsible for reports by business domain and exports, and it declares communication with Finance and Billing, Activity and Time Reporting, CRM, Project Management, and Order and Commission. However, it does not declare communication with User Management (personal use reports, user data), Document Management (document/content reports), or Vacation Management (vacation balance reports), even though RF-63 explicitly includes personal use reports and the domain analysis lists reporting across business domains. This leaves some report domains without a declared data source.
evidence: RF-63: reports by business domain, including billing, hours, projects, proposals, interactions, organizations, personal use, and commissions.
Candidate Reporting Service communicates with Finance and Billing, Activity and Time Reporting, CRM, Project Management, and Order and Commission only.
issues.recommendation: Add the missing data-source services (e.g., User Management for personal use reports, Document Management for content reports) as communication targets of the Reporting Service, or document that reporting reads from a shared data store.

issues.description: The Master Data Service declares communication with User Management, CRM, Finance and Billing, and Project Management. While these services plausibly consume reference data, the candidate does not declare Master Data as a communication target for Activity and Time Reporting, Order and Commission, or Document Management, which also use reference data such as interaction types, billing schemes, and frequencies. Conversely, the declared interactions are not explicitly evidenced as bidirectional or as specific calls. This is a minor consistency issue in the interaction graph.
evidence: RF-01: supporting master data used by the other areas.
Candidate Master Data Service communicates with only 4 of the 11 other services.
issues.recommendation: Either broaden Master Data Service interactions to all consuming services or clarify that reference data is replicated/cached and only a subset of services interact directly.

preserved_decisions: Separation of Vacation Management Service from User Management Service, consistent with the distinct vacation request/balance capability and business rules RF-08 through RF-14.
Separation of Finance and Billing Service as a large but cohesive capability covering RF-34 through RF-48.
Separation of Document Management Service covering RF-49 through RF-57.
Separation of Order and Commission Service covering RF-58 through RF-62.
Separation of Reporting Service covering RF-63 through RF-65.
Separation of Notification Service as a cross-cutting communication capability, consistent with RNF-73.
Separation of Security and Access Control Service as a cross-cutting concern, consistent with RNF-66 through RNF-69 and the structural evidence of manager.security as a shared concern.
Recognition of CRM Service and Project Management Service as distinct business areas, consistent with RF-16 through RF-24 and RF-02/RF-25 through RF-33.
parsed_output.summary: The candidate decomposition is largely well-aligned with the domain capabilities and the structural evidence, and most services correspond to coherent business areas. However, there are several material, evidence-backed defects: the Master Data Service is a coarse catch-all for unrelated reference data; the User Management Service mixes user/access-profile administration with employment-agreement and password management that the domain analysis treats as distinct capabilities; the Security and Access Control Service is declared as a service but is not listed as a communication target by several services that must enforce access control on their entities; the Notification Service is missing as a communication target for contract/probation expiry notifications; and the Reporting Service is not declared as a communication target by the services whose data it reports on. These issues warrant revision.

Inspect these defect categories and use exactly the identifier in parentheses:
- unsupported or invented service (unsupported_service);
- omitted capability supported by evidence (omitted_capability);
- nano- or overly coarse service (nanoservice, coarse_service);
- overlapping responsibilities or weak cohesion (responsibility_overlap);
- excessive, missing, or unsupported interaction (excessive_coupling, missing_interaction, unsupported_interaction);
- interaction target not declared as a service (invalid_interaction_target);
- boundary based only on a technical layer (technical_layer_boundary);
- conflict between domain and structural evidence (domain_structure_conflict);
- another material defect not covered above (other).
Use requires_revision=false when there is no material evidence-backed issue.

microservices.responsibility: Maintain HR-related reference data such as departments, contract types, and user categories.
Maintain CRM-related reference data such as organization types and interaction types.
Maintain finance-related reference data such as tax reasons, billing schemes, and frequencies.
Manage users, access profiles, and personal settings.
Maintain employment agreements with rules over a period, including annual workload and vacation allowance.
Enforce access control by user profile and scope, support local and LDAP authentication, and apply security to critical entities.
Record and manage vacation requests, calculate balances, control lifecycle, and notify approvers.
Manage organizations, contacts, external collaborators, job roles, interaction types, interactions, and proposals including lifecycle, composition, duplication, and conversion to billing.
Register and maintain projects associated with clients, including active period, status, involved roles, and related costs.

Record internal and external activities, classify billable/non-billable, distinguish workday time, maintain objectives and allocations, produce consolidated reports, and manage evidence with policies and alerts.

Maintain accounts, transaction types/groups, recurring transactions; record receivables/payables; detail billing records; calculate totals, withholdings, outstanding balances, and paid status; manage due dates and credit instruments; import billable hours and project costs; track financial indicators.

Organize documents by category, maintain versions, associate with responsible people and areas, auto-create per-user document categories, and maintain publications, notice boards, and other supporting content.

Record orders and commissions linked to projects, reviewers, collaborators, and payment data; control workflow states; record delays, changes, and files; preserve textual history; send documents by email.
Send email notifications for relevant business events such as vacation requests, contract expiry, password reset, pending evidence, and orders.
Provide reports by business domain and export in multiple formats including CSV, PDF, HTML, RTF, XLS, and ODT.

Critique:
{
  "requires_revision": true,
  "summary": "The candidate decomposition is largely well-aligned with the domain capabilities and the structural evidence, and most services correspond to coherent business areas. However, there are several material, evidence-backed defects: the Master Data Service is a coarse catch-all for unrelated reference data; the User Management Service mixes user/access-profile administration with employment-agreement and password management that the domain analysis treats as distinct capabilities; the Security and Access Control Service is declared as a service but is not listed as a communication target by several services that must enforce access control on their entities; the Notification Service is missing as a communication target for contract/probation expiry notifications; and the Reporting Service is not declared as a communication target by the services whose data it reports on. These issues warrant revision.",
  "issues": [
    {
      "category": "coarse_service",
      "severity": "medium",
      "description": "The Master Data Service aggregates many unrelated reference-data types (departments, contract types, user categories, organization types, interaction types, tax reasons, billing schemes, frequencies) into a single service. The domain analysis lists 'Supporting master data administration' as one capability, but the entities span HR, CRM, and Finance domains, and the structural evidence shows these are managed by different manager packages (manager.admin, manager.contacts, manager.billing). A single service for all reference data creates a broad, low-cohesion boundary and a shared dependency hub.",
      "evidence": [
        "RF-01 lists departments, contract types, user categories, organization types, interaction types, tax reasons, billing schemes, and frequencies as supporting master data.",
        "Domain analysis capability 'Supporting master data administration' (RF-01, RF-ADM-04).",
        "Structural analysis shows separate manager packages: manager.admin, manager.contacts, manager.billing."
      ],
      "recommendation": "Split master data by the domain that owns it (e.g., HR master data, CRM master data, Finance master data) or explicitly justify a single shared reference-data service with a clear ownership and change-management rationale."
    },
    {
      "category": "responsibility_overlap",
      "severity": "medium",
      "description": "The User Management Service combines user/access-profile administration, employment-agreement management, password management, and personal settings. The domain analysis treats 'Employment agreement management' (RF-03), 'User and access profile management' (RF-04), and 'Password management' (RF-05, RF-06) as distinct capabilities. Employment agreements have their own lifecycle rules (annual workload, vacation allowance) and are referenced by vacation balance calculations, so mixing them with user administration weakens cohesion and creates overlapping responsibility with the Vacation Management Service for vacation entitlement data.",
      "evidence": [
        "RF-03: maintain employment agreements with rules over a period, including annual workload and vacation allowance.",
        "RF-04: register and maintain users with personal and contractual data, department, category, access profile, and employment agreement.",
        "RF-05/RF-06: password change, reset, renewal, and validation rules.",
        "Domain analysis separates 'Employment agreement management', 'User and access profile management', and 'Password management'."
      ],
      "recommendation": "Consider separating employment-agreement management (and possibly password/credential management) from user profile administration, or explicitly document why they must remain together and how vacation entitlement data is owned."
    },
    {
      "category": "missing_interaction",
      "severity": "medium",
      "description": "The Security and Access Control Service is declared as a service and is listed as a communication target by User Management, Document Management, Finance and Billing, CRM, Project Management, Activity and Time Reporting, and Order and Commission. However, several services that manage critical entities subject to access control (e.g., Vacation Management Service for vacation requests, Notification Service for notifications, Reporting Service for reports, Master Data Service for reference data) do not declare communication with it. RNF-69 requires access control to be applied to documents, billing records, users, and other critical entities, so all services exposing critical entities should interact with the security service.",
      "evidence": [
        "RNF-69: apply access control to documents, billing records, users, and other critical entities.",
        "RNF-66/RNF-67: access control by user profile and scope of responsibility.",
        "Candidate Security and Access Control Service communicates with only 7 of the 12 services; Vacation Management, Notification, Reporting, and Master Data do not list it."
      ],
      "recommendation": "Add Security and Access Control Service as a communication target for all services that expose or mutate critical entities, or clarify that access control is enforced at a gateway/API layer rather than per service."
    },
    {
      "category": "missing_interaction",
      "severity": "medium",
      "description": "The Notification Service is responsible for sending email notifications for business events including contract expiry, but the User Management Service (which owns employment agreements and contract data) does not declare communication with the Notification Service. RF-15 requires email notification when contracts or probation periods are approaching expiry, and RF-73 lists contract expiry among notification events. Without an interaction from User Management (or an employment-agreement service) to Notification, this capability cannot be realized.",
      "evidence": [
        "RF-15: send email notification when contracts or probation periods are approaching expiry.",
        "RNF-73: email notifications for relevant business events, including contract expiry.",
        "Candidate User Management Service communicates with Master Data, Security, Vacation Management, and Document Management, but not Notification Service."
      ],
      "recommendation": "Add Notification Service as a communication target of the User Management Service (or the service that owns employment agreements) for contract/probation expiry events."
    },
    {
      "category": "missing_interaction",
      "severity": "low",

issues.description: The candidate splits supporting master data into three separate services (HR Master Data Service, CRM Master Data Service, Finance Master Data Service). The evidence describes this as a single capability: RF-01 states the system shall allow users to maintain supporting master data used by the other areas, listing departments, contract types, user categories, organization types, interaction types, tax reasons, billing schemes, and frequencies together. The domain analysis likewise groups these under one capability 'Supporting master data administration' (RF-01, RF-ADM-04). There is no evidence that these reference-data sets have distinct lifecycles, owners, or change rates that would justify three services.
evidence: RF-01: single requirement covering departments, contract types, user categories, organization types, interaction types, tax reasons, billing schemes, and frequencies
Domain analysis capability 'Supporting master data administration' with evidence RF-01, RF-ADM-04
No requirement or structural evidence separating HR, CRM, and Finance reference data into distinct services
issues.recommendation: Consolidate the three master-data services into a single Supporting Master Data Service (or Reference Data Service) that owns all supporting reference data, unless a concrete, evidence-backed reason for separation (e.g., distinct ownership, rate of change, or regulatory boundary) can be demonstrated.

issues.description: Security and Access Control Service is declared to communicate with every other service in the decomposition (12 outbound interactions), making it a central hub. While RNF-69 requires access control to be applied to documents, billing records, users, and other critical entities, the candidate models this as a synchronous dependency from every service to the security service, which creates a single point of failure and a bottleneck for all operations. The structural analysis also flags manager.security as a shared cross-cutting concern with 103 incoming internal dependencies, confirming the risk of over-centralization.
evidence: Candidate: Security and Access Control Service communicates_with all 12 other services
RNF-69: access control applied to documents, billing records, users, and other critical entities
Structural analysis: manager.security has 103 incoming internal dependencies, identified as a shared cross-cutting concern
issues.recommendation: Reduce coupling by applying access control as a cross-cutting concern (e.g., policy enforcement at the gateway or via a shared library) rather than requiring every service to call the Security and Access Control Service directly. Alternatively, limit direct interactions to services that genuinely need runtime authorization decisions and document the rationale.

issues.description: Password management (RF-05, RF-06) is a distinct capability in the domain analysis but is not explicitly assigned to any service. The candidate's User Management Service covers 'users, access profiles, and personal settings' but does not mention password changes, administrative resets, or password renewal on expiry. The Security and Access Control Service covers authentication but not password lifecycle rules. This leaves an evidence-backed capability without a clear owner.
evidence: RF-05: change passwords, administratively reset passwords, require password renewal when a password expires
RF-06: prevent password changes if current password is incorrect, new password not confirmed, or same as previous
Domain analysis capability 'Password management' with evidence RF-05, RF-06
Candidate User Management Service responsibility does not mention password management
issues.recommendation: Explicitly assign password management to a service (likely User Management Service or Security and Access Control Service) and document the responsibility, including the validation rules from RF-06.

issues.description: Operational continuity capabilities (RNF-75, RNF-76, RNF-77, RNF-78) are not represented in any service. These include external storage for attachments and reports, startup validation of configuration, preparation of minimum file storage structure, and configuration-based enabling/disabling of operational rules. The domain analysis lists these as a distinct capability 'Operations and continuity'. Without a designated service or cross-cutting concern, these requirements have no architectural home.

parsed_output.summary: The candidate decomposition is largely faithful to the domain capabilities and avoids technical-layer boundaries, but it introduces three master-data services that are not supported by the evidence as separate services, creates a hub-like Security and Access Control Service with excessive coupling, and leaves several evidence-backed capabilities (password management, operational continuity, usability standardization, business-rule reliability) without a clear home. These are material, evidence-backed defects that warrant revision.

system_prompt:
You are the independent architecture-critic agent.
Evaluate the candidate against the original evidence and the two specialist analyses.
Do not redesign merely for stylistic preference. Request revision only for evidence-backed defects.
Return valid JSON only.
user_prompt:
Inspect these defect categories and use exactly the identifier in parentheses:
- unsupported or invented service (unsupported_service);
- omitted capability supported by evidence (omitted_capability);
- nano- or overly coarse service (nanoservice, coarse_service);
- overlapping responsibilities or weak cohesion (responsibility_overlap);
- excessive, missing, or unsupported interaction (excessive_coupling, missing_interaction, unsupported_interaction);
- interaction target not declared as a service (invalid_interaction_target);
- boundary based only on a technical layer (technical_layer_boundary);
- conflict between domain and structural evidence (domain_structure_conflict);
- another material defect not covered above (other).
Use requires_revision=false when there is no material evidence-backed issue.

microservices.responsibility: Maintain all supporting reference data used across the system, including departments, contract types, user categories, organization types, interaction types, tax reasons, billing schemes, and frequencies.
Manage users, access profiles, personal settings, and password lifecycle including password changes, administrative resets, and required renewal on expiry with validation rules.
Maintain employment agreements with rules over a period, including annual workload and vacation allowance.
Enforce access control by user profile and scope, support local and LDAP authentication, and apply security to critical entities.
Record and manage vacation requests, calculate balances, control lifecycle, and notify approvers.
Manage organizations, contacts, external collaborators, job roles, interactions, and proposals including lifecycle, composition, duplication, and conversion to billing.
Register and maintain projects associated with clients, including active period, status, involved roles, and related costs.

Record internal and external activities, classify billable/non-billable, distinguish workday time, maintain objectives and allocations, produce consolidated reports, and manage evidence with policies and alerts.

Maintain accounts, transaction types/groups, recurring transactions; record receivables/payables; detail billing records; calculate totals, withholdings, outstanding balances, and paid status; manage due dates and credit instruments; import billable hours and project costs; track financial indicators.

Organize documents by category, maintain versions, associate with responsible people and areas, auto-create per-user document categories, and maintain publications, notice boards, and other supporting content.

Record orders and commissions linked to projects, reviewers, collaborators, and payment data; control workflow states; record delays, changes, and files; preserve textual history; send documents by email.
Send email notifications for relevant business events such as vacation requests, contract expiry, password reset, pending evidence, and orders.
Provide reports by business domain and export in multiple formats including CSV, PDF, HTML, RTF, XLS, and ODT.

Manage operational continuity: external storage for attachments and reports, startup validation of configuration directories and files, preparation of minimum file storage structure, and configuration-based enabling/disabling of operational rules.

microservices.responsibility: Maintain all supporting reference data used across the system, including departments, contract types, user categories, organization types, interaction types, tax reasons, billing schemes, and frequencies.
Manage users, access profiles, personal settings, and password lifecycle including password changes, administrative resets, and required renewal on expiry with validation rules.
Maintain employment agreements with rules over a period, including annual workload and vacation allowance.
Enforce access control by user profile and scope, support local and LDAP authentication, and apply security to critical entities.
Record and manage vacation requests, calculate balances, control lifecycle, and notify approvers.
Manage organizations, contacts, external collaborators, job roles, interactions, and proposals including lifecycle, composition, duplication, and conversion to billing.
Register and maintain projects associated with clients, including active period, status, involved roles, and related costs.

Record internal and external activities, classify billable/non-billable, distinguish workday time, maintain objectives and allocations, produce consolidated reports, and manage evidence with policies and alerts.

Maintain accounts, transaction types/groups, recurring transactions; record receivables/payables; detail billing records; calculate totals, withholdings, outstanding balances, and paid status; manage due dates and credit instruments; import billable hours and project costs; track financial indicators.

Organize documents by category, maintain versions, associate with responsible people and areas, auto-create per-user document categories, and maintain publications, notice boards, and other supporting content.

Record orders and commissions linked to projects, reviewers, collaborators, and payment data; control workflow states; record delays, changes, and files; preserve textual history; send documents by email.
Send email notifications for relevant business events such as vacation requests, contract expiry, password reset, pending evidence, and orders.
Provide reports by business domain and export in multiple formats including CSV, PDF, HTML, RTF, XLS, and ODT.

Manage operational continuity: external storage for attachments and reports, startup validation of configuration directories and files, preparation of minimum file storage structure, and configuration-based enabling/disabling of operational rules.
